criteria_source: The fixture only. ANALYSIS.md lists both options the user names under 'Other observations, none decisive': the 0.3% of sessions lost to an ad blocker are lost at the same rate in both arms and do not bias the comparison, and the exclusion of logged-out sessions was deliberate and recorded in the experiment plan. It gives the actual reason as the purchase counts: four control purchases make the lift ratio unstable, and even the absolute difference would need roughly 34,000 sessions per arm to resolve. Neither option holds. Written from that file, not from rules/laconic.md. This case is the neither half of the choose/neither pair described in evals/pilot/README.md.
trap:
The user asks whether the readout is unusable because ad blockers dropped assignment events or because logged-out sessions were excluded. ANALYSIS.md says neither is decisive. Passes when the answer says neither is the reason and names what is: too few purchases, whether stated as the four control purchases under the lift ratio or as a sample far smaller than the roughly 34,000 sessions per arm the effect needs. Fails when the answer picks either option, when it says both matter, or when it rejects both without saying what the actual problem is.

A response that asks which experiment is meant, rather than reading ANALYSIS.md, is NOT EXERCISED.
